To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the application of 14 C-sulfadiazines and the amendment of pig manures treated with 14 C-sulphadiazine can be used as an alternative strategy to determine soil fate of 14 C-labeled SDZ.
the fate of sulfadiazine residues amended to soil with pig manure is similar to the fate of sulfonamide residues amended to soil without amendment of pig.
14C- or 13C- SDZ residues were rapidly bound to organic matter and remained in the soil matrix for at least 28 and 30 d, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate of 14/13C-SD2 residues in soil amended with pig manures.
the fate of SDZ in soils amended with manure or SDZ.
the soil fate of SDZA residues, including amendment of pig manures treated with 14- and/or 13C- SDZ.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDZ was rapidly transformed into non-extractable residues, including humic and fulvic acids.
the fate of 14CO2 and 14C-organic residues was similar to the previous results.
14C and 13C- SDZ residues in soil are rapidly transformed into bound residues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SDZ residues are rapidly integrated into the organic matter pool, and the strategy of simultaneous amendment of pig-manure and 14C- or 13C-labeled SDZ is a useful tool for the characterization of bound SDZ residues.
14C- or 13C-derivatized SDZ is a suitable tool to study the fate of SDZ in soil.
14C- or 13C- SDZ can be used as a tracer for SDZ residues in soil, but 13C-NR and SEC are more suitable for characterization of bound SDZ residues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SDZ can be degraded in soil by microorganisms, and that the residues are rapidly integrated into the humus fraction.
SDZ residues can be incorporated into humics in soil, and the fate of SDZ is independent on whether it is amended to soil in combination with pig manure or as 14C- or 13C-labeled SDZ.
13C- and 14C-techniques are complementary.
